newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Greece will not be letting up the pressure on economic policy in the wake of the French victory in Sunday's national elections, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou was quick to point out yesterday. "We are a leftist government which has achieved an increase in real incomes and stability in employment," he said.
--The administration of the Commercial Bank is working out how it can distribute free shares to shareholders from the capitalisation of reserves.

--The government's amendment on changes to lump sum payments to pensioners in the public sector is based on union recommendations and is not expected to cause industrial unrest within the ranks of public servants.
--OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, is entering the final stretch in negotiations to buy a 20 percent stake in the Serbian telecoms organisation. Sources say the purchase is a "good" buy.

--The establishment of a derivatives market will turn a new page for the capital market. Yesterday, Papandoniou presented the draft bill on the market which also foresees reforms to the running of the stock exchange.
--The Social Security Foundation (IKA) will borrow 84 billion drachmas from other state-run pension funds to pay pensions, according to reports.
-- Third party insurance premiums for cars are expected to double in the next few years although there is expected to be a drop in parameters for other policies.
--Institutional investors from abroad have invested in the National Bank's 200 million dollar bond loan, issued yesterday on international markets.

--A final decision on whether the government will cave in the European Commission demands to lift special charges on imported secondhand cars - as well as to other issues affecting the car market - will be taken in the autumn, according to the national economy and finance minister.
--There's concern at the national economy and finance ministry about the viable changes it is able to make to the tax collection mechanism.
--Procedures for the listing of 10 percent of the share capital of DEP, the natural gas company, on the Athens Bourse are on the move.
